Around the world, scholarship programs play an important role in helping students gain access to education, especially those who face financial difficulties. As scholarship programs continue to expand, many governments and educational institutions have turned to web-based and automated systems to manage applications, records, and communication more effectively. Research shows that automating these processes helps reduce manual workload, minimize errors, improve transparency, and ensure that information is delivered to applicants in a timely and organized manner (Al-Ayyubi & Maulana, 2023).

, Local Government Units (LGUs) actively support education by offering locally funded scholarship programs. The Municipality of San Enrique, Negros Occidental reflects this commitment by providing financial assistance to qualified students. However, the current scholarship process still depends largely on manual practices such as posting announcements on social media, using handwritten application forms, maintaining records in spreadsheets, and requiring physical submission of documents. Studies indicate that these manual methods often lead to delays, miscommunication, repeated submissions,
and difficulties in monitoring and retrieving scholarship records (

To respond to these challenges, this study proposes the development of a web-based Automated Scholarship Records Management System for the LGU of San Enrique, Negros Occidental. The proposed system is designed to centralize scholarship records, streamline application processing, track application status, and improve communication through SMS notifications. While physical document verification remains necessary for accounting, auditing, and approval purposes, the system aims to improve efficiency, transparency, and accessibility, resulting in a more organized and reliable scholarship management process for both LGU staff and scholarship applicants.

The Automated Scholarship Records Management System for the LGU of San Enrique, Negros Occidental, will benefit the following:
To The LGU Of San Enrique.

This study will provide a more efficient and accurate system for managing scholarship records, reducing administrative workload and improving overall program administration. It will enable faster processing of applications, better tracking of student data, and streamlined communication with scholars.
To The Scholarship Applicants and Scholars.

This study will provide a more accessible and transparent platform for accessing scholarship information and application forms. It will also facilitate timely communication regarding application status and scholarship updates, reducing the need for frequent visits to the LGU office.

This study will serve as a valuable reference for future researchers interested in developing similar scholarship management systems or other local government management systems. It will provide insights into the challenges and solutions involved in automating administrative processes.

This study focuses on the design, development, and implementation of a web-based Automated Scholarship Records Management System for the Local Government Unit (LGU) of San Enrique, Negros Occidental. The system covers online scholarship announcements, applicant registration, digital application submission, document uploading and monitoring, application status tracking, and SMS notifications with mobile number verification through

. It also supports bulk SMS sending for scholarship announcements, interview schedules, approval notices, and disbursement updates. Additionally, the system includes applicant and scholar record management, interview scheduling, approval monitoring, and the recording of scholarship disbursement details.

The system is designed to support the existing scholarship process of the LGU and is accessible to scholarship applicants, LGU staff, and administrators. It aims to improve efficiency, organization, communication, and record management by centralizing scholarship data and reducing reliance on purely manual procedures. However, the system does not replace government-mandated processes such as physical document submission, verification, accounting review, auditing, and approval by authorized offices. These procedures remain manual and are only supported by the system through digital pre-screening, bulk notifications, and record organization.
This study is limited by factors such as the accuracy of data entered by users and the availability of internet connectivity for online access,

SMS delivery. The system does not handle actual financial transactions or provide real-time chat between applicants and LGU staff; communication is limited to system notifications and individual or bulk SMS alerts. Furthermore, the system is developed specifically for the LGU of San Enrique, Negros Occidental and is not intended for use by other LGUs without further customization.

REVIEW OF RELATED LITERATURE AND SYSTEMS

This chapter presents the related literature, studies, and systems that are pertinent to this study. The present study is anchored on these related literature and systems which give relevant information and better enlightenment for the readers to understand clearly the development of an Automated Scholarship Records Management System for the LGU of San Enrique, Negros Occidental. This review explores existing scholarship management approaches, the automation of administrative tasks in LGUs or similar institutions, and the application of web-based technologies and notification systems in such contexts.
QR-Code Tracking and SMS Notification Transaction Interface for Scholarship Management System
, K. A., Sermeno, J. P., and

, N. E. (2021) developed a system which aimed to address issues in tracking and communication within the scholarship processing workflow. Implemented at the University of Antique, the system was specifically designed to improve the handling of scholarship documentation by incorporating QR code functionality to streamline document verification and enable accurate, real-time tracking of submitted requirements. Additionally, SMS notifications were integrated to provide timely updates to scholars regarding their application status and document verifications.

The researchers reported that the system significantly reduced administrative delays and human errors in document handling. It also improved transparency by keeping scholars informed about their application progress. In relation to the present study, this system demonstrates how technology can be leveraged not only for data storage but also for real-time communication and efficient document monitoring. These features are highly relevant to the proposed Automated Scholarship Records Management System for the LGU of San Enrique, which similarly aims to incorporate document tracking and notification features to reduce miscommunication, delays, and redundant follow-ups between the LGU and its scholars.

Commission on Higher Education (CHED) introduced the TES Tracker System in 2021 as a digital tool to monitor the distribution of Tertiary Education Subsidy (TES) stipends, particularly in the Davao Region. This system enables real-time tracking of fund disbursement to grantees by requiring scholarship coordinators to regularly update an online form with details such as the number of beneficiaries and the amounts released. This initiative aligns with the objectives of the proposed Automated Scholarship Records Management System for the LGU of San Enrique, Negros Occidental. Both systems aim to enhance transparency, efficiency, and accountability in scholarship management through digital solutions. By adopting similar real-time monitoring and data updating features, the LGU's system can ensure timely fund
distribution and accurate record-keeping, thereby improving service delivery to scholarship beneficiaries.

Blancaflor et al. (2022) created a web-based system which aimed to improve how students apply for scholarships at the tertiary level. The system was developed in response to the growing number of applications and the need to make the process more organized and efficient. It allowed students to apply online and enabled administrators to evaluate and manage applications more easily. Based on user feedback through a usability survey, the system was found to be effective and easy to use. The researchers also recommended adding mobile access and SMS features in future versions. This study supports the current research, as it shares the same goal of digitizing scholarship processes. Just like
, the proposed system for the LGU of San Enrique aims to reduce manual work, improve access, and simplify scholarship tracking for both students and administrators.
Designing a Web-Based Information System for Scholarship Management: Supporting Access and Rapid Dissemination of Information

The development of web-based information systems for scholarship management is a crucial area of focus for improving the efficiency and effectiveness of scholarship programs (Al-Ayyubi & Maulana, 2023). As indicated in the study, there is a recognized need to move away from traditional, manual processes towards centralized, automated

platforms. Such systems aim to streamline the management of scholar information, including applications and administrative tasks, by providing centralized data storage, facilitating online application processing, automating record-keeping, and enhancing communication between stakeholders. These objectives closely align with the goals of the proposed Automated Scholarship Records Management System for the LGU of San Enrique, which seeks to address similar inefficiencies through the development of a web-based solution.
Web-Based Monitoring Information System for scholarship

et al (2020) addresses the challenges of monitoring scholarship recipients in an institution, Universitas Muhammadiyah Magelang. The traditional method of collecting hard files face-to-face led to data loss and duplication. The related study emphasized the need for automated systems to improve data management, reduce data loss and duplication, and facilitate communication between stakeholders. Similarly, the proposed study aims to automate and enhance scholarship processes for the LGU of San Enrique, Negros Occidental through a web-based platform.
Optimizing scholarship distribution: a management information system approach.
et al., (2024) introduced a web-based Management Information System (MIS) designed to optimize scholarship distribution for a philanthropic institution in Indonesia. The system featured

automated scholar profiling, academic performance monitoring, document tracking, and real-time report generation—functions that directly align with the goals of the present study. Specifically, the MIS addressed inefficiencies in manual processing, delayed reporting, and a lack of transparency, which are also challenges identified in the current scholarship operations of the LGU of San Enrique. By centralizing scholarship data and enabling quota monitoring, the system supported fair and data-driven allocation of funds,
what the proposed LGU system aims to achieve.

The study by Khelifi et al. (2023) introduced a Smart Scholarship System aimed at streamlining the scholarship application and management process at Abu Dhabi University (ADU). This system addressed challenges such as the need for physical presence during applications, non-specific scholarship systems, and time-consuming application reviews. Key features

enabling students to apply for various scholarships online, verify their application status, update personal data, and receive administrative assistance through live chat. These functionalities align closely with the objectives of the proposed Automated Scholarship Records and Management System for the LGU of San Enrique, which seeks to enhance efficiency, transparency, and accessibility in scholarship management through automation and centralized data handling.

utilized. For the Automated Scholarship Records Management System, a mixed-methods approach will be adopted for data collection, primarily utilizing survey questionnaires and structured interviews.
The instrument was divided into two (2) parts. The first part collected

basic demographic information relevant to the study, such as the respondent's role (LGU Staff, Scholarship Applicant) and, if applicable, their level of experience with similar systems. Personal identification like names will be optional to ensure anonymity and encourage candid responses. The second part included the questions
designed to assess various aspects of the A
. The questions were structured using the Likert Scale. The Scale was used to validate the effectiveness, usability, sustainability and maintainability of the system.
The researchers will gather primary data by first submitting a formal letter to the LGU of San Enrique to request permission and seek approval for conducting

the study. Upon approval, LGU staff involved in the scholarship program and scholarship applicants will be identified and selected as respondents. Throughout the process, ethical conduct will be paramount, ensuring informed consent is secured from all participants, and maintaining the confidentiality and anonymity of their responses. The survey questionnaires and interview guides will then be finalized and, if feasible, pilot-tested to ensure clarity and relevance.
